items.title: Anwar: World needs fairer financing system to avoid unsustainable debt
items.summary: Anwar said the call was important as the world faced rapid changes in the economic and geopolitical landscape, as well as technological developments. He said many developing countries continued to struggle to achieve economic progress. "As such, the international financing system must be fairer and must not push countries into unsustainable debt simply to meet the basic needs of their people," he said in a Facebook post.

items.title: Helicopter crash: 'I prayed it was not him,' schoolmate grieves for Zainol Afiq
items.summary: His worst fears were confirmed the following day when a message in their school WhatsApp group identified 30-year-old Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham as one of those killed in the crash. "But the next day, it was confirmed in our school WhatsApp group that one of the victims was Zainol Afiq. Dr Fauzan remembered Zainol Afiq as someone who was always willing to help others.

items.title: Former minister Jamil Khir to face three charges over Tabung Haji probe tomorrow
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — Former minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom is reportedly set to be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow in connection with an investigation into Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) arising from a Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). According to Bernama , the court system showed that Jamil Khir is scheduled to appear before Sessions Court judge Rosli Ahmad at 9am. Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman reportedly said on Thursday that the commission had recommended three charges against the former minister under Section 403 of the Penal Code for dishonest misappropriation of property.

items.title: Trump turns to golf, family business on Irish visit's second day
items.summary: DOONBEG (Ireland): Donald Trump turned his focus Sunday to golf and promoting his business interests, as he wraps up a two-day visit to Ireland during which his off-the-cuff diplomacy has caused another stir. The US president caught his Irish hosts and the neighbouring UK off-guard Saturday when he waded into highly sensitive political territory by announcing he would "love to see" a united Ireland. "Donald Trump is Donald Trump and the president will say and speak his mind as he sees it," UK minister Angela Rayner told Sky News on Sunday.

items.title: After BRICS Summit, Anwar arrives in Keralam for second leg of India working visit
items.summary: KERALAM, INDIA: After attending the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim arrived in Calicut, also known as Kozhikode, Keralam (renamed from Kerala), today for the second and final leg of his working visit to India. Anwar was received by the Consul General of Malaysia to South India K. Saravana Kumar, Consul General of Malaysia in Mumbai Najwa Musyrifah Ramli, Keralam Agriculture Minister T. Siddique and Keralam Chief Secretary Bishwanath Sinha. Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied on the working visit by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.

items.title: Flying Doctor Service suspension to remain pending helicopter crash probe
items.summary: The Health Ministry said the temporary suspension of FDS operations would remain in place pending the outcome of the investigation, with the safety and welfare of healthcare workers remaining its top priority. The ministry said it was carrying out a comprehensive audit covering service-location mapping, compliance by the operating company with required standards and the psychosocial needs of FDS personnel. In the meantime, the ministry said it was putting alternative arrangements in place to minimise the impact of the suspension on healthcare access in remote areas.

items.title: MOH assures healthcare access will continue in rural Sarawak after suspension of Flying Doctor Service
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) has assured that access to healthcare services for rural communities in Sarawak will continue following the temporary suspension of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) operations in the state. In a statement today, MOH said the suspension involved seven FDS teams covering 85 locations with an estimated population of 14,830 people in remote areas. “To ensure continuity of treatment, MOH is reassessing healthcare service programmes for each location based on accessibility and local conditions.

items.title: Police confirm probe into three policemen over alleged RM13,000 extortion
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Police confirmed they are investigating three policemen for allegedly extorting RM13,000 from several men in Pulau Tikus here on Aug 6. Penang police chief Datuk Dennis Lim said the trio, aged between 30 and 48, were detained yesterday and remanded for four days until Sept 16 to assist investigations. The case is believed to have involved the complainant and three of his cousins, who went to Jalan Ladang Hong Seng, Pulau Tikus, at about 2.30am to look for a friend's relative who was allegedly detained by police.

items.title: Philippine ferry fire victims may take months to identify
items.summary: CORON: Authorities in the Philippines said on Sunday it could take weeks or months to identify the victims of a ferry fire that killed 76 people, as forensic experts begin collecting and comparing DNA samples from charred remains and investigators determine what caused one of the country's deadliest maritime disasters in recent years. "It could be weeks, or it could be much longer." Officials said more remains could still be found because investigators have not yet fully searched flooded sections of the vessel.

items.title: Indonesia says six killed, 130 missing after ferry capsizes off Java
items.summary: BANJARMASIN (Indonesia): Rescuers in Indonesia said at least six people were killed and 130 others were missing on Sunday after a ferry sailing between the islands of Java and Borneo was hit by bad weather and capsized. Basarnas, Indonesia's national search and rescue agency, said in its latest update that six people were killed and 130 were missing. It said 107 people had been rescued.

items.title: Motorcyclist arrested after ramming traffic policeman in Kota Tinggi
items.summary: KOTA TINGGI: A motorcyclist allegedly rammed into a traffic policeman who stopped him for riding without a helmet here today, leaving the officer with a fractured right hand. The 24-year-old man was arrested shortly after the 10.03am incident during a traffic operation targeting motorcyclists by the district police traffic investigation and enforcement division. District police chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the operation targeted motorcyclists who had committed traffic offences, including riding without helmets.

items.title: [UPDATED] Jamil Khir to be charged tomorrow over Tabung Haji RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Former minister in the prime minister's department Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom will be charged tomorrow over a case linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) on Sept 10 confirmed that a former minister would be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court tomorrow. Meanwhile, in a statement today, MACC said it had obtained approval to prosecute the former minister.

items.title: Parliament Open Day draws record 13,368 visitors
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The two-day Parliament Open Day which began yesterday successfully attracted over 13,368 visitors, exceeding the initial target of 10,000 people. Parliament staff brief visitors inside the Dewan Rakyat and Dewan Negara on the final day of the Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026 in Kuala Lumpur on September 13, 2026. Visitors take a closer look at the Parliament lobby during the Malaysia Parliament Open Day 2026 in Kuala Lumpur on September 13, 2026.

items.title: Serian, three Sarawak areas record unhealthy API readings
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Four areas in Sarawak recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 6pm today, with Serian recording the highest reading in the country at 174 amid the ongoing haze. Meanwhile, 48 stations recorded moderate API readings, while seven recorded good air quality. API readings of 0 to 50 indicate good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous.

items.title: Thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds forecast in seven states and KL until 9pm
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds in seven states and the Federal Territory of Kuala Lumpur until 9pm today. In a statement, MetMalaysia said other areas affected are in Kedah (Kulim, Bandar Baharu, Baling and Sik) and Perak (Hulu Perak, Selama and Muallim). The same warning has been issued for Tumpat, Kota Bharu, Bachok and Pasir Puteh in Kelantan, while in Terengganu, the areas involved are Hulu Terengganu, Marang, Kuala Terengganu, Kuala Nerus, Setiu and Besut.

items.title: Anwar: No country should have to choose between repaying debt and caring for its people
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called for a fairer global financing system, saying no country should be forced to choose between repaying its debts and meeting its obligations to its people. “No nation should be forced to choose between honouring its debts and honouring its obligations to its people,” he said when delivering his speech at the National Statement on Shaping the Future for Inclusive Global Growth at the end of the 18th Brics Leaders Summit here today. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said financing must be “fit for purpose”, stressing that meeting basic needs and providing public goods should not leave countries with unsustainable debt.

items.title: Man hospitalised after unknown assailant stabs him at KL Wholesale Market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — A man in his 30s was injured in the back after being stabbed with a sharp metal object by an unidentified individual at the Kuala Lumpur Wholesale Market yesterday. Sentul acting district police chief Supt Jasni Zolpa said the incident occurred at about 8.40am while the man was working at the market. The victim's friend also lodged a police report about the incident at 1.30pm today.

items.title: PN to focus efforts on 126 'winnable' parliamentary seats ahead of GE16
items.summary: PN information chief Tan Sri Annuar Musa said that number, however, did not include seats in Sarawak. He said, while Pas may not contest all 126 seats, the party was ready to provide support and assist "like-minded allies" contesting in those constituencies. "Although Pas will not necessarily contest all 126 seats, it is Pas' principle and practice to assist like-minded allies who contest in those seats later," he said in a Facebook post.

items.title: Man stabbed in back by unknown assailant at Kuala Lumpur market
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A man in his 30s suffered a stab wound to the back after being attacked with a sharp metal object by an unidentified person at the Kuala Lumpur Wholesale Market yesterday. Sentul acting district police chief Superintendent Jasni Zolpa said the incident occurred about 8.40am while the man was working at the market. The victim's friend also lodged a police report about 1.30pm today.

items.title: ‘This may be my last time’: Abang Johari hints at possible final term as PBB president, calls on younger leaders to step up
items.summary: MIRI, Sept 13 — “This may be my last time.” That was the candid message from Premier Datuk Patinggi Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg as he called on the older generation to make way for younger leaders to carry on the responsibility and struggle of Parti Pesaka Bumiputera Bersatu (PBB). The PBB president said leadership succession was a natural process and that the party must continuously prepare and train younger members to take over when the time came.

items.title: Thailand weighs flat 450-baht entry fee for foreign visitors by 2027
items.summary: BANGKOK: The Thai government is currently conducting a public consultation on a proposed tourism fee of 450 baht (approximately RM55.35) for all foreign visitors. According to Minister Surasak Phancharoenworakul, the proposed rate is a flat 450 baht per person, regardless of whether visitors arrive by air, land, or sea. Last year, Thailand welcomed approximately 33 million foreign tourists, which could generate an estimated 14.8 billion baht for the tourism fund.

items.title: Anglers find barrel with suspected human remains near Machap Water Reservoir
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH, Sept 13 — A barrel believed to contain human remains was found on a slope by the roadside near the Machap Water Reservoir here today, according to Alor Gajah police chief Supt Ahmad Abu Bakar. He said the blue barrel was found by three anglers aged between 25 and 35 while fishing at the reservoir at about 11.40am. Ahmad said initial investigations found that the remains were believed to have been decomposing for at least three weeks.

items.title: BRICS offers economic opportunities, reduces Western market dependence, says Anwar
items.summary: NEW DELHI: BRICS offers significant geoeconomic advantages in several areas, creating critical mass through a large integrated market and opening up opportunities to diversify trade, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said this would enable BRICS member economies to reduce their heavy dependence on traditional Western markets. Anwar also said Malaysia maintained that sovereignty must be respected, civilians must be protected and global economic arteries must be kept away from the battlefield.

items.title: Anwar heads to Keralam for final leg of India visit after Brics summit
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim departed for India’s Southern State, Keralam (renamed from Kerala) for his second and final leg of his working visit in India after participating in the 18th Brics’ Leaders Summit here. The aircraft carrying the Prime Minister departed the Air Force Station (AFS) Palam, New Delhi at 2.15pm local time (4.45pm Malaysian Time) to Kozhikode (Calicut), Keralam. As part of the visit, the Prime Minister is scheduled to meet the Chief Minister Thiru V. D. Satheesan and Governor of Kerala Thiru Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar.

items.title: Queen visits man who lost wife, two sons in Kluang house fire
items.summary: KLUANG: Her Majesty Raja Zarith Sofiah, Queen of Malaysia, today visited a man who lost his wife and two sons in a devastating house fire in Taman Titiwangsa here. Her Majesty, accompanied by Her Highness Tunku Mahkota Johor Che' Puan Mahkota Khaleeda Bustamam, visited Khairul Nizam Wahid, 50, and offered support and aid to the grieving family. Raja Zarith Sofiah and Che' Puan Khaleeda also visited three other recipients and presented them with aid during their visit to the district.

items.title: After toddler attack, Batu Pahat steps up stray dog crackdown
items.summary: The Batu Pahat Municipal Council (MPBP) has captured 736 stray dogs in 205 operations this year, following 1,557 captures in 263 operations last year. MPBP has also intensified efforts to remove roaming dogs from high-risk areas. This followed 1,557 dogs captured in 263 operations throughout last year.

items.title: Home minister: New deputy IGP chosen after consultation with King, announcement due soon
items.summary: KULIM, Sept 13 — The appointment of the new deputy inspector-general of police (IGP) has been finalised and will be announced soon, said Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail. Saifuddin Nasution said several names had been considered and discussions held before the process was finalised. On the eligibility criteria for the deputy IGP post, Saifuddin Nasution said all officers holding the rank of police commissioner (CP) were eligible for consideration.

items.title: Lim Guan Eng calls for unity to counter PAS and Umno’s racial, religious politics
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — DAP chairman Lim Guan Eng has called on Malaysians to unite against what he described as the “dangerous brand of extremist politics” projected by PAS and Umno following their respective party gatherings. In a written statement today, Lim said the conclusion of the PAS Muktamar and Umno General Assembly had projected politics centred on religious and racial dominance without respecting the “basic spirit and fundamental tenets” of the Federal Constitution and the rule of law. Lim proposed 10 areas that he said could help counter PAS and Umno while fostering national unity in Malaysia’s multiracial society and greater integration between Sabah, Sarawak and Peninsular Malaysia.

items.title: 30 inmates find purpose through Quran memorisation programme in Machang
items.summary: MACHANG: Thirty inmates at Machang Rehabilitation Centre are taking part in a structured tahfiz programme, with two having completed memorising all 30 juzuk of the Quran and another two expected to do so by year-end. "Currently, 30 inmates are taking part in the programme. Zulkarnain said the programme was part of efforts to provide inmates with a meaningful rehabilitation process by combining correctional programmes with religious education.

items.title: Iraq to reopen Iran crossings after drone attack
items.summary: BAGHDAD: Iraqi authorities announced on Sunday a timeline to reopen three crossings with Iran, a day after closing them following a drone attack originating from their shared border on a Saudi pipeline. Two Iraqi security sources told AFP on Saturday that drone launchers were found near the al-Shib border crossing in Missan. The government's security media cell said Sunday that "after reviewing operations at the border crossings," they would gradually reopen for passengers and trade on a timeline from Sunday until Thursday.

items.title: Kota Bharu police seek man seen kicking young girl in restaurant CCTV video
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Police have opened an investigation paper in connection with a viral video showing a man kicking a young girl at a well-known Thai restaurant in Telipot here. Kota Bharu police chief ACP Mohd Azmir Damiri said police received a report from a member of the public at about 10.24pm today regarding the video, which went viral on the Threads social media platform. “The video shows the rough behaviour of a man kicking a young girl believed to be his daughter at a well-known Thai restaurant in Telipot.

items.title: Iran authorities say one dead after ship struck in Hormuz
items.summary: TEHERAN: A ship was struck in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday, killing one person and injuring three, local Iranian authorities said, as Teheran and Washington clash over the strategic waterway. Several explosions were reported overnight around Qeshm, the largest island in the Hormuz strait. The UK Maritime Trade Operations monitor said later it had received reports of a vessel being struck by an unknown projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz.

items.title: Remains of Captain Zainol Afiq arrive at Bandar Baru Senawang mosque
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The remains of helicopter crash victim Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham arrived at Bandar Baru Senawang Mosque here about 4.20pm today. Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan was also at the mosque, arriving at about 4.15pm. Traffic police were deployed to manage traffic, while Seremban district police chief Assistant Commissioner Mohd Yatim Osman and his personnel monitored the situation.

items.title: Helicopter crash: Remains of Dr Ainul Baraah laid to rest in Pengkalan Chepa
items.summary: KOTA BARU: A sombre atmosphere enveloped the burial of medical officer the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Sri Kedeper Islamic Cemetery in Pengkalan Chepa here today. Also present were Health Ministry secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased's family members and friends. Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah's remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at the Sultan Ismail Petra Airport in Pengkalan Chepa, Kota Bharu, at 11.21am.

items.title: Saifuddin welcomes Umno commitment to stay in unity government
items.summary: KULIM: Umno's commitment to remain in the unity government until the end of its term is a positive development to ensure political stability, economic growth and efforts to address the people's problems remain priorities, a Pakatan Harapan leader said. PH secretary-general Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi's stance was in line with the memorandum of understanding signed between the parties in 2022 to form the unity government. He also said political attacks between leaders of both parties were normal and could be resolved ahead of the election.

items.title: Dzulkefly leads 1,000 congregants in funeral prayers for Dr Ainul Baraah
items.summary: KOTA BARU: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad led the funeral prayers for medical officer, the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here at 1.37 pm today. The prayers were attended by over 1,000 congregants, including Ministry of Health (MOH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan State Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased's family members and friends. Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah's remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at Sultan Ismail Petra Airport, Pengkalan Chepa, at 11.21 am.

items.title: APEC ministers push for greater energy security in Asia Pacific
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Asia Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) energy ministers are pushing to strengthen energy security across Asia Pacific as rising electricity demand puts greater pressure on power systems, costs and supply chains. "The Asia Pacific accounts for roughly 60 per cent of global energy production and consumption. "Strengthening energy cooperation is directly relevant not only to each economy's own development but also carries significant weight for the global energy landscape."

items.title: Skeleton found inside water drum at Durian Tunggal Dam
items.summary: ALOR GAJAH: Skeletal remains believed to be human were found inside a water drum at the Durian Tunggal Dam catchment pond here at noon. Alor Gajah District Police Chief Superintendent Ahmad Abu Bakar said the identity of the skeleton has yet to be established. He said police are investigating to determine the cause of death and how the remains ended up inside the drum.

items.title: Lebuh Pudu raid uncovers suspected clinics serving foreigners
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: At least four premises suspected of illegally selling and storing medicines, including two operating like makeshift clinics for foreigners, were uncovered during a massive Immigration Department-led operation in Lebuh Pudu today. The suspected clinics, concealed behind businesses selling textiles and offering travel services, were equipped with devices used to conduct blood pressure, blood sugar and blood tests. Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Health Department Pharmacy Enforcement Branch chief Shafilliza Samsuri said various medicines without Health Ministry approval were seized from the premises.

items.title: Zahid has 3 options to challenge unity government
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Pasir Gudang MP Hassan Abdul Karim said Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has three options if he wishes to challenge the unity government without waiting for the prime minister to take action to remove the party from the coalition. He said all three options had parliamentary channels available and did not require Zahid to wait for Anwar to dismiss Umno ministers or remove the party from the government. At the same time, Anwar is someone who is indebted to Umno and would not have the heart to dismiss Umno ministers or remove the party from the government.

items.title: PKNPk sharpens pupils' digital skills
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Perak State Development Corp (PKNPk) continues to strengthen digital literacy and modern media skills among primary school students through its StratCom Jr. Programme. The programme, conducted in collaboration with Sekolah Kebangsaan St. Michael (SKSMI), Ipoh, aims to equip students and teachers with digital communication, critical thinking and media production skills. PKNPk chief executive Datuk Redza Rafiq Abdul Razak said early exposure to media and communication skills was important in building a strong foundation in media literacy and critical thinking.

items.title: Mujahid ready to assist MACC probe into Tabung Haji RCI findings
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Former minister Datuk Seri Dr Mujahid Yusof Rawa said he was ready to assist investigations into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH). Mujahid, who was the minister overseeing religious affairs in 2018, said he had no problem providing investigators with whatever information he knew about the issues raised in the RCI report. Mujahid, who is also Amanah deputy president, said nearly half of the 14 cases referred for action in the RCI report had already been known when he headed the ministry in 2018, during efforts to rehabilitate TH.

items.title: Malaysia’s Brics partnership broadens trade ties while keeping ‘middle path’, says J-KOM
items.summary: GOPENG, Sept 13 — Malaysia’s participation as a Brics partner opens up wider trade opportunities with member countries that collectively represent more than half of the world’s population and purchasing power. “With Brics, we can balance our trade with various other countries. “The 11 Brics member countries are official members.

items.title: FDS crash: Dr Ainul’s husband thanks all, calls nationwide support a ‘blessing’
items.summary: Muhammad Faiz Abdul Malik, 37, said the support from the federal, Sarawak and Kelantan governments had greatly helped facilitate arrangements concerning his late wife, including throughout his time in Sarawak. Thank you to everyone, including the media,” he told reporters when met at Masjid Al Karomah Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here today. Dr Ainul Baraah, 33, was laid to rest at the Sri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery at 2.20pm today following funeral prayers at Masjid Al Karomah Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa.

items.title: MOH to review all FDS helicopter contracts, RM30 flight allowance after fatal Sarawak crash
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) will review all contracts related to helicopter services for the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) following the crash of an FDS helicopter in Long Lellang, Baram, Sarawak, last Tuesday. Health director-general Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said the review would cover all aspects of the contracts, including matters related to FDS, in line with instructions from Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad. Following the crash, MOH announced that FDS operations in Sarawak would be temporarily suspended to allow a comprehensive assessment of the service's safety and operational mechanisms.

items.title: EC to review electoral boundaries nationwide if Parliament approves more Sabah, Sarawak seats
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 13 — The Election Commission (EC) will conduct a review of electoral constituency boundaries, subject to amendments to the Federal Constitution. EC chairman Datuk Seri Ramlan Harun said it took note of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s statement on Friday on the proposed amendments to the Federal Constitution to allow for an increase in the number of parliamentary seats for Sabah and Sarawak. “In the context of the delineation of electoral constituencies in the three study units, the EC will conduct a review of the electoral constituency boundaries, subject to amendments to the Federal Constitution,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Police, RMAF among four agencies supporting Sarawak during Flying Doctor Service suspension
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Four enforcement agencies will assist the Ministry of Health (MOH) in carrying out mercy flights to aid people in remote areas of Sarawak who require medical assistance. The four agencies are the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), the Malaysian Maritime Enforcement Agency (MMEA), and the Fire and Rescue Department of Malaysia (JBPM). “The mobilised alternatives include securing assistance from JBPM through its Emergency Medical Air Rescue Services (EMARS).

items.title: Anwar: 1MDB recovery about restoring trust amid RM4.2b claim against Singapore’s DBS
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Finance (MoF) has taken note of a compensation claim amounting to approximately RM4.2 billion filed by four companies against DBS Bank Ltd at the Singapore High Court. The MoF statement also said that, according to the 1MDB Asset Recovery Task Force, the claim involves five DBS accounts opened in 2013 by the four companies. The accounts were allegedly used to channel more than US$1 billion (RM4.07 billion) in misappropriated 1MDB and SRC funds between 2013 and 2014.

items.title: Construction of Cameron Highlands bypass yet to begin, suspension calls premature, says Works Ministry
items.summary: KUANTAN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Works (KKR) has taken note of media reports and concerns raised regarding flash floods and landslides in Cameron Highlands, including calls for the temporary suspension of the Cameron Highlands Bypass Project. In a statement today, the Public Works Department (JKR) explained that the project involves the construction of the Tanah Rata Bypass, the upgrading of Federal Road FT59 from Tanah Rata to Kea Farm, and the upgrading of Federal Road FT434 (Jalan Griddle). “Therefore, any claims linking the flash flood incident to the project's physical construction activities are inaccurate,” the statement read.

items.title: Health Minister leads funeral prayers for helicopter crash victim Dr Ainul Baraah
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Sept 13 — Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad led the funeral prayers for medical officer, the late Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin, 33, at Al Karomah Mosque in Mukim Baung Besar, Pengkalan Chepa, here at 1.37 pm today. The prayers were attended by over 1,000 congregants, including Ministry of Health (MOH) secretary-general Datuk Seri Hasnol Zam Zam Ahmad, Kelantan Menteri Besar Datuk Mohd Nassuruddin Daud, Kelantan State Health director Dr Kasuadi Hussin, as well as the deceased’s family members and friends. Earlier, a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft carrying Dr Ainul Baraah’s remains from Miri, Sarawak, arrived at Sultan Ismail Petra Airport, Pengkalan Chepa, at 11.21 am.

items.title: Fisherman missing after falling into sea near Pulau Batu Layang found dead
items.summary: KANGAR, Sept 13 — The body of a fisherman who fell into the sea while fishing near Pulau Batu Layang, Sungai Baru here yesterday, was found about 400 metres from the island today. Kuala Perlis Maritime Zone director Maritime Commander Nak Rong A/L Si Prom said the body was discovered by local fishermen and the finding was reported to the search and rescue operation team this morning. “The operation team received information from the fishing community about the discovery of a body approximately 400 metres from Pulau Batu Layang,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: Health Ministry preparing for possible rise in public hospital patients amid soaring insurance costs
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Sept 13 — The Ministry of Health (MOH) is constantly planning and projecting healthcare service requirements to prepare for a possible increase in the number of patients at public hospitals amid rising health insurance costs. Director-General of Health Datuk Dr Mahathar Abd Wahab said such planning and projections formed part of the public healthcare sector’s day-to-day and long-term planning, including financial requirements to meet changes in demand for healthcare services. Dr Mahathar said the ministry was also aware of concerns over reported increases of up to 20 per cent annually in health insurance costs, which could place a greater financial burden on the public and affect demand for public healthcare services.

items.title: Anwar confirms Malaysia exploring acquisition of India’s BrahMos missile system
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim confirmed that Malaysia is exploring the possibility of acquiring India’s BrahMos air-to-surface missile system, while emphasising that discussions are still ongoing and no final decision has been made. In an interview with India’s NDTV, he said discussion on it took place during the bilateral meeting with his Indian counterpart, Narendra Modi, but the rightful decision maker would be Malaysia’s Air Force. Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, acknowledged India’s defence capabilities.

items.title: Health Ministry seeks to close trauma care gaps between peninsula, Sabah and Sarawak
items.summary: He said the trauma chain of survival must be strengthened comprehensively, from bystander response and first aid at the scene to pre-hospital emergency medical services and transportation, resuscitation at the Emergency Department, definitive trauma care and rehabilitation. He said access to quality trauma care should not depend on a patient’s location, as every Malaysian deserved timely and appropriate trauma care. Meanwhile, he said up to 30 per cent of trauma deaths were considered preventable based on the first National Trauma Registry report published in 2008.

items.title: Teen among 146 detained in road bully operation at Bukit Raja toll plaza
items.summary: Sinar Harian reported that the integrated operation involving the Selangor Traffic Investigation and Enforcement Department (JSPT), Road Transport Department (JPJ) and National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) also resulted in 50 motorcycles being seized for various offences. In a statement, Selangor police said 146 individuals aged between 16 and 25, as well as 141 motorcycles, were inspected during the operation. “Selangor police issued 92 summonses, while the Bukit Aman JSPT issued 24 summonses for various traffic offences,” the statement said.

items.title: Motorcyclist dies after trying to avoid pedestrian in Hulu Selangor
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Sept 13 — A 60-year-old motorcyclist died after he reportedly tried to avoid a pedestrian crossing the road before falling and being run over by a lorry in Hulu Selangor yesterday. Sinar Harian reported that the incident occurred at about 7pm along Jalan Batang Kali-Ulu Yam, citing Hulu Selangor district police chief Supt M Manimaran. Manimaran said preliminary investigations found that the victim was believed to have been overtaking a lorry from the right when a pedestrian was crossing the road.

items.title: Police investigate death of 15-year-old girl after fall from Putrajaya apartment
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Sept 13 — Police are investigating the death of a 15-year-old girl who was found on the ground of an apartment in Precinct 5 here after she was believed to have fallen from a high floor of the building, Putrajaya District Police Chief ACP Aidi Sham Mohamed said today. He said police received a call about the incident at 10.33pm yesterday and the girl was pronounced dead at the scene by a medical officer from Putrajaya Hospital. “Preliminary investigations found that the 15-year-old girl was found lying down, believed to have fallen from a high place.

items.title: Health Minister: FDS crash victims’ remains handed over to families after DNA identification
items.summary: Health Minister Datuk Seri Dzulkefly Ahmad said the Ministry of Health (MOH) coordinated the transportation of the remains to their respective final resting places following official confirmation of their identities by the police and the Department of Chemistry. He said the remains of medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamarudin will be flown from Miri to Kota Bharu, Kelantan on a Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) special aircraft before being buried at Seri Kedeper Muslim Cemetery, Kampung Baung, Pengkalan Chepa. “The remains of assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry would be taken to his family home today, with the funeral scheduled for Tuesday (Sept 15) at Anglican Cemetery Lambir, Miri,” he said in a statement.

items.title: Police shoot at car after couple allegedly try to ram traffic officers, detained within 24 hours
items.summary: KULAI, Sept — Police fired one shot at the tyre of a car after a 23-year-old couple allegedly rammed a police motorcycle and tried to hit officers during an incident in Jalan Kenari, Bandar Putra, Kulai, early yesterday. Kulai District Police Chief ACP Tan Seng Lee said the incident occurred at about 1.20 am when members of the district police headquarters’ Motorcycle Patrol Unit (URB) stopped a black Perodua Myvi in the area after finding it suspicious, with a local man and woman inside the vehicle. Tan said within 24 hours of the incident, Kulai police arrested the male and female suspects separately in Bandar Putra, Kulai and Kluang between 11.30 am and 8.30 pm yesterday.

items.title: Anwar says Egypt’s El-Sisi to make official visit to Malaysia next month
items.summary: NEW DELHI, Sept 13 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said Egyptian President Abdel Fattah El-Sisi is scheduled to make an official visit to Malaysia next month. “Insya-Allah, several matters concerning Malaysia-Egypt relations will be discussed in greater depth during President El-Sisi’s official visit to Malaysia next month,” he said in a post on his social media today. This is Anwar’s second official visit to India, following his inaugural trip as Prime Minister in August 2024.
